# New renderings, iliad-155 (24.302–404)

Rows in the format of the table in conventions.md: Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ἀμφίπολον ταμίην (24.302) | "the attendant housekeeper" | "the attendant housekeeper" | "handmaid", "maid" (reserved for δμῳή); follows the Odyssey table's ἀμφίπολος "attendant" and ταμίη "housekeeper" |
| ἀκήρατον (ὕδωρ, 24.303) | "pure" | "pure" | "unpolluted", "unmixed", "clean"; derivation not certain, so the plain "pure" |
| χέρνιβον · πρόχοον (24.304) | "washing-basin" · "pitcher" | "washing-basin" · "pitcher" | "ewer" (kept for the pitcher), "water for washing" (the note says the first word may mean the water) |
| ἧς ἀλόχοιο (24.305) | "from his own wife" | "from his wife" | ἧς is the possessive "his own", kept apart from the relative |
| φίλον ἐλθεῖν ἠδ’ ἐλεεινόν (24.309) | "to come to Achilles dear and pitiable" | "to come to Achilles as one dear to him and worthy of his pity" | "welcome and pitied" (decides φίλος as "welcome"), "friendly"; ἐλεεινός "pitiable" |
| ὣς ἔφατ’ εὐχόμενος, τοῦ δ’ ἔκλυε μητίετα Ζεύς (24.314, whole line) | "So he spoke, praying, and him heard counsellor Zeus," | "So he prayed, and Zeus the counsellor heard him," | follows the table's Phoebus Apollo row and μητίετα Ζεύς "counsellor Zeus" / "Zeus the counsellor" |
| μόρφνον … περκνόν (24.316) | "the morphnos … the perknos" | "the morphnos … the perknos" (+ note: names of a kind of eagle; μόρφνος unknown, περκνός "dusky") | "dusky", "dark-spotted" (each silently picks a sense), "black eagle" |
| θηρητήρ (24.316) | "hunter" | "hunter" | "huntsman", "predator" |
| ἐῢ κληῗσ’ ἀραρυῖα (24.318, of a door) | "well fitted with bolts" | "well fitted with its bolts" | "bars", "locks"; follows the table's κληΐς "bolt" (21.236) and ἀραρυῖα "fitted" |
| ὑψορόφοιο θύρη θαλάμοιο (24.317) | "the door of a high-roofed chamber" | "the door of a rich man’s high-roofed chamber" | "lofty", "high-ceilinged"; follows the table's ὑψόροφος "high-roofed" |
| εἴσατο (24.319, aorist of εἴδομαι) | "appeared" | "showed itself" | "seemed", "went" (the other verb εἶσα, "sent"), "saw" |
| σπερχόμενος (24.322) | "hurrying" | "in haste" | "urgently", "unceasingly" (reserved for ἀσπερχές) |
| τετράκυκλον ἀπήνην (24.324) | "the four-wheeled wagon" | "the four-wheeled wagon" | "four-wheeled cart", "carriage"; follows the table's ἀπήνη "wagon" |
| μάστιγι κέλευε (24.326, of a driver and horses) | "kept bidding on with the whip" | "pressed on with his whip" | "ordered" (kept for κελεύω of persons), "urged on" (reserved for ὀτρύνω), "drove" (reserved for ἐλαύνω) |
| φίλοι (24.327, subject of ἕποντο) | "dear ones" | "dear ones" | "friends", "kinsmen" (each decides which) |
| γαμβροί (24.331) | "sons-in-law" | "sons-in-law" (+ note: can mean other relatives by marriage) | "kinsmen by marriage", "brothers-in-law" |
| προφανέντε (24.332, dual) | "having come into view" | "as they came into view" | "appearing", "showing themselves" |
| υἱὸν φίλον (Ἑρμείαν, 24.333) | "his dear son" | "his dear son" | "his own son"; φίλον is the possessive "his own dear" |
| ἑταιρίσσαι (24.335) | "to be a companion to" | "to be a companion to" | "befriend", "keep company with" (reserved for ὀπηδέω), "act as comrade" |
| ἐριούνιος (24.360) | "the helper" | "the helper" (+ note: meaning unknown; "helper" is one ancient guess) | follows the table's ἐριούνης "the helper"; "luck-bringer", "the runner" (each picks one guess) |
| κούρῳ αἰσυμνητῆρι (24.347) | "a young prince" | "a young prince" | "a young ruler", "a young umpire"; αἰσυμνητήρ is rare and its sense here is taken from context |
| βῆ δ’ ἰέναι (24.347) | "he set out to go" | "set out on his way" | "went to go", "hastened" |
| μέγα σῆμα … Ἴλοιο (24.349) | "the great tomb of Ilus" | "the great tomb of Ilus" | "sign", "mound" (see the table's σῆμα "tomb") |
| τὸν δ’ ἐξ ἀγχιμόλοιο ἰδών (24.352) | "from close by seeing" | "saw him from close by" | "from near", "from a short way off" |
| φάτο φώνησέν τε (24.353) | "he said, and lifted his voice" | "said … lifting his voice" | "spoke and called", "said aloud"; follows the table's φωνήσας "lifting his voice" |
| φραδέος νόου ἔργα τέτυκται (24.354) | "of a shrewd mind the works are at hand" | "this is work for a shrewd mind" (+ note: literal sense and the usual sense) | "the deeds of a wise mind are done", "a clever scheme is afoot", "be wary" (each decides the thought); φραδής "shrewd" |
| διαρραίσεσθαι (24.355) | "to be torn apart" | "to be torn to pieces" | "to be destroyed", "to be cut down"; διαρραίω "tear to pieces, shatter" |
| ἐφ’ ἵππων φεύγωμεν (24.356) | "let us flee on the horses" | "let us flee with the horses" | "on horseback" (they are in a chariot) |
| λιτανεύσομεν (24.357) | "we shall beseech" | "beg" | "implore" (kept for γουνάζομαι), "supplicate"; the note says the form may be a subjunctive |
| σὺν … νόος χύτο (24.358) | "with the old man his mind was poured together" | "the old man’s wits were thrown into confusion" | "his mind was gone", "he lost his wits" (decides the degree); συγχέω "pour together, confuse" |
| ὀρθαὶ δὲ τρίχες ἔσταν (24.359) | "upright stood the hairs" | "the hairs stood upright" | "his hair bristled", "his hair stood on end" (modern idiom); γναμπτοῖσι μέλεσσι keeps "pliant" (l) / "supple" (i) of the table |
| ταφών (24.360) | "in amazement" | "in amazement" | follows the table's ταφών "in amazement" |
| νύκτα δι’ ἀμβροσίην (24.363) | "through the ambrosial night" | "through the ambrosial night" | "divine night", "the night of the gods"; follows the table's ἀμβροσίη νύξ |
| ἰθύνεις (24.362) | "you steer" | "you are steering" | "drive" (reserved for ἐλαύνω), "direct" |
| δυσμενέες καὶ ἀνάρσιοι (24.365) | "ill-disposed and hostile" | "ill-disposed and hostile" | "enemies"; the two words kept apart as in the table |
| θοὴν νύκτα μέλαιναν (24.366) | "swift black night" | "swift black night" | "dark", "quick" |
| ὀνείατα (24.367) | "helpful things" | "helpful things" | "delicacies" (the table's ὀνείατα μυρία of food), "goods", "valuables", "treasure" (κειμήλια); ὄνειαρ "a help" |
| τίς ἂν δή τοι νόος εἴη; (24.367) | "what then would your mind be?" | "what would you then think?" | "what would you say", "what would your plan be" |
| γέρων … ὀπηδεῖ (24.368) | "old is this one who keeps you company" | "the man who keeps you company is old, too old to ward off a man" | "attends", "accompanies"; ὀπηδέω "keep company with"; the note says the infinitive is one of result with "too old" unsaid |
| ἄλλον σεῦ ἀπαλεξήσαιμι (24.370) | "I would ward off another from you" | "I would keep another away from you" | "defend you against", "fight off"; ἀπαμύνασθαι "ward off" kept for the other verb |
| τὸν δ’ ἠμείβετ’ ἔπειτα γέρων Πρίαμος θεοειδής (24.372, 24.386, whole-line reply-formula) | "Him then answered the old man Priam, godlike in form:" | "Then Priam, the old man, godlike in form, answered him:" | "king Priam", "godlike" flat; follows the table's τὸν δ’ ἠμείβετ’ ἔπειτα and θεοειδής rows |
| οὕτω πῃ τάδε γ’ ἐστί (24.373) | "Thus in some way these things are" | "So it is" | "somehow it is so"; πῃ is the softening indefinite adverb, not repeated in `i` |
| ὑπερέσχεθε χεῖρα (24.374) | "has held his hand over" | "has held his hand over" | "protected", "stretched out his hand"; the image is a shield held above |
| ὁδοιπόρον … αἴσιον (24.375–376) | "wayfarer … auspicious" | "traveller … a good omen" | "journeyer", "favourable" (reserved for the αἶσα-family "fitting" of ἐναίσιμος); αἴσιος "auspicious" |
| δέμας καὶ εἶδος ἀγητός (24.376) | "in body and form admirable" | "admirable in build and in looks" | "handsome", "wondrous"; ἀγητός "admirable", δέμας "build" |
| πέπνυσαι νόῳ (24.377) | "you are prudent in mind" | "prudent in mind" | "wise", "sensible"; follows the table's πεπνυμένος "prudent" |
| τὸν δ’ αὖτε προσέειπε διάκτορος ἀργεϊφόντης (24.378, 24.389, whole-line speech introduction) | "Him then in turn addressed the guide, Argeïphontes:" | "Then the guide, the slayer of Argus, said to him in turn:" | "answered" (reserved for ἠμείβετο); follows the table's 21.497 row |
| ἠέ … ἦ ἤδη … (24.381, 24.383) | "whether … or by now …" | "whether … or whether by now …" | a direct question ("Are you sending … or …?"), because the unit before ends with a colon after "tell me" |
| ἐκπέμπεις κειμήλια (24.381) | "you are sending out treasures" | "you are sending your many good treasures out" | "valuables", "heirlooms"; follows the table's κειμήλια "treasures" |
| ἄνδρας ἐς ἀλλοδαπούς (24.382) | "to foreign men" | "to foreign men" | "strangers", "to another land" (reserved for ξένος) |
| σόα (24.382) | "safe" | "safe" | "sound", "unharmed" |
| τοῖος γὰρ ἀνὴρ ὤριστος ὄλωλε (24.384) | "for such a man, the best, has perished" | "for such a man, the best, has perished" | "the best of men" (loses the demonstrative τοῖος), "died" (ὄλωλε is "has perished") |
| οὐ μέν τι μάχης ἐπιδεύετ’ Ἀχαιῶν (24.385) | "in no way was he lacking in battle with the Achaeans" | "he was in no way lacking in battle against the Achaeans" | "he lacked nothing in fighting" (drops Ἀχαιῶν), "was inferior to the Achaeans" (a second reading of the genitive) |
| φέριστε (24.387, vocative) | "best of men" | "best of men" | follows the table's φέριστε |
| ὥς μοι καλὰ τὸν οἶτον ἀπότμου παιδὸς ἔνισπες (24.388) | "how finely the fate of my ill-fated son you have told me" | "How well you have told me of the fate of my ill-fated son!" | "doomed", "luckless", "unfortunate"; ἄποτμος "ill-fated"; οἶτος "fate" as in the table |
| πειρᾷ ἐμεῖο (24.390) | "you make trial of me" | "you are testing me" | "you tempt me", "you try me"; πειράω "try, test" |
| μάχῃ ἔνι κυδιανείρῃ (24.391) | "in the man-glorifying battle" | "in the battle that brings men glory" | follows the table's μάχην κυδιάνειραν (4.225) |
| κτείνεσκε δαΐζων (24.393) | "he kept killing, cutting them down" | "kept killing them, cutting them down" | "slaying", "hewing"; the -σκε form is a past habitual |
| ἑσταότες θαυμάζομεν (24.394) | "standing by, we marvelled" | "we stood by and marvelled" | "wondered", "gazed"; follows the table's θάμβος "wonder"; the present is read as a vivid past |
| κεχολωμένος Ἀτρεΐωνι (24.395) | "being angered at the son of Atreus" | "angry with the son of Atreus" | "enraged", "wrathful" (reserved for μῆνις / μήνιος) |
| μία δ’ ἤγαγε νηῦς εὐεργής (24.396) | "one ship brought me, a well-made one" | "one well-made ship brought me" | "good ship", "strong ship"; follows the table's εὐεργής "well-made" |
| Μυρμιδόνων δ’ ἔξειμι (24.397) | "Of the Myrmidons I am" | "I am one of the Myrmidons" | "I come from" (could suggest the future of ἐξέρχομαι); ἐξ εἰμί "I am of" |
| Πολύκτωρ (24.397) | "Polyctor" | "Polyctor" | "Polyktor"; the name of a Myrmidon father, in the Greek only here |
| παλλόμενος κλήρῳ λάχον (24.400) | "the lot being shaken, I obtained by lot" | "when lots were shaken among us brothers, I drew the lot" | "I cast lots" (decides who shakes); the note says the grammar is loose |

| ἀσχαλόωσι … καθήμενοι (24.403) | "chafe, sitting" | "sit and chafe" | follows the table's ἀσχαλάω "chafe"; "grow restless" |
| ἴσχειν ἐσσυμένους πολέμου (24.404) | "to hold back those eager for war" | "hold back their men, who are eager for war" | "restrain", "check"; ἐσσυμένους "eager", with "their men" supplied in `i` for the unstated object |

## Departures and reuse notes

- No departure from a published Iliad unit: 24.306 (partly), 24.308, 24.311–312, 24.315, 24.321, 24.379 and 24.380 take the published English, adjusted only where the surrounding sentence differs (24.311 "you" for "him", 24.312 first person).
- Odyssey lines 24.339, 24.340–342, 24.343–345, 24.348 and 24.369 take the Odyssey English as shipped. The sandal lines (24.340–342) and the wand lines (24.343–344) end here in a semicolon or ano teleia as printed, so the final stop of the shipped English is changed to match. ἀμβρόσια (24.341) is "immortal" as in the Odyssey's same lines, though ἀμβρόσιος elsewhere in the Iliad is "ambrosial" (the table); noted in the unit's note.
- The packet's Greek for 24.308, 24.315 and 24.343 prints no comma at the line end where the published units show one (the edition's text, not a copying error); `t` follows the packet.
